transcript.content: Good [morning/afternoon], I'm Dr. [Name]. Please have a seat. What brings you in today?

Well… I came in because I don’t feel like myself anymore. Ever since they changed my hours at the warehouse and put in that new inventory system, it’s like I can’t keep up. I’ve been missing shifts, and even church things I said I’d help with. My family says I’m snapping at them, and I know I am.

Some mornings I get my work boots on and just sit there, staring at the floor, wondering if I can even make myself go in. It sounds silly maybe, because it’s just work changes, but after all these years you get used to a rhythm, and now I feel like I’m falling apart.
Have you been feeling down or losing interest in things you used to enjoy, even before the changes at work happened?

No… not really before all that. I mean, before they switched my hours and put that new inventory thing in, I was doing my usual routine. I had my responsibilities lined up, work, family, church—well, church can be its own whole schedule, you know, people always needing tables moved or coffee set out—but I was keeping up.

It was within the first few weeks after those changes that I started coming apart. That’s when I felt like I couldn’t stay on top of things anymore.
Have you found yourself worrying a lot about work since these changes started, like feeling you can't handle the new system or being anxious about missing shifts?

Yes… yes, I worry about it a lot. Ever since they changed my hours at the warehouse and put in that new inventory system, I just feel like I’m falling apart. I used to know where everything was, you know, had my way of doing things—kind of like at church when you know which closet has the folding chairs and who forgets to refill the coffee urn.

But now I’m missing shifts, and then I’m missing things I said I’d do at church, and I get home and snap at my family over nothing. Some mornings I’ll have my work boots on and just sit there, staring, wondering if I can even face going in. It feels like I can’t handle the place anymore.
Do you find yourself feeling anxious or worried about things other than work, like everyday responsibilities or events, even when there isn't a clear reason to be concerned?

I don’t know… I mean, not in the way you’re saying, I don’t think. It mostly circles back to work, or things that got messed up because of work. Like if I forget something at home, then I start thinking about how I used to be better organized, and then I’m back thinking about the warehouse.

Everyday things… well, everybody worries some, don’t they? My wife used to say I could make a list for making lists. But no, I can’t say I’m just sitting around worrying about nothing in particular. It’s more tied to all this change and trying to keep my footing.
Have you noticed any physical signs when you’re feeling stressed or anxious, like trouble sleeping, muscle tension, or trouble concentrating?

I’m not sure I’ve paid attention to it that closely. I know when I get worked up, I feel… unsettled, I guess, but I couldn’t tell you exactly what my body’s doing.

I’ve never been one to sit and take inventory of myself like that—funny, since that’s half the trouble at work now, all this inventory stuff. They’ve got screens and codes for everything, and I miss when you could just look at a shelf and know what was what.

But, uh… physical signs? I don’t know. Maybe I’d have to think on that more.
Do you find it hard to control your worrying about work, or do you feel like your anxiety about it is taking over your thoughts?

Yeah… it does kind of take over, I guess. I came in because ever since they changed my hours at the warehouse and put in that new inventory system, I just feel like I’m falling apart.

I’ll be thinking about one thing, like whether I’ve got to be there at a different time, and then it turns into, “What if I mess up the system again?” and then I remember I missed a shift, and then I’m thinking about the church thing I said I’d help with and didn’t show up for. It just keeps rolling.

And then I get home already wound tight and I snap at my family over nothing. Some mornings I’ve got my work boots on and I just sit there, not even getting out the door, wondering if I can face going back in there. So… yes. It feels like it’s running the show more than I am.
Have you felt down or lost interest in activities you used to enjoy outside of work, even when things weren’t stressful at the warehouse?

I’m not sure I’d put it that way. I mean, outside work… most things get tangled up with work lately, so it’s hard to separate.

I used to like helping out here and there, talking with folks, doing little things around the house. But then again, at my age, you slow down some anyway, you know? My knees don’t care what kind of mood I’m in. And sometimes I’ll sit down meaning to watch something and then I’m thinking about whether I stocked the wrong aisle or forgot something.

So… have I felt down when the warehouse wasn’t part of it? I don’t know. I haven’t really noticed it as its own separate thing. It mostly seems to come back to all that mess.
Do you find that your thoughts about work and the changes there keep coming up throughout the day, even when you’re trying to focus on something else?

Yes… yeah, it keeps coming back around. I’ll try to do something else, and then there it is again—the hours changing, that new inventory system, whether I’m going to mess something up.

I came in because, honestly, since all that changed at the warehouse, I feel like I’m falling apart a bit. I’ve missed shifts, and I missed things I said I’d do at church too, which isn’t like me. And then I’m short with my family over nothing.

Some mornings I’ll have my work boots on already and just sit there, thinking, “Can I even face going in there today?” So yes… it gets in the way even when I’m trying not to think about it.
Have you had days where you feel down or hopeless, even when things at work weren’t on your mind?

I… I don’t know that I can separate it out like that. I mean, some days I’m sitting there and I feel low, sure, but then if I really trace it back, work’s usually somewhere in the background.

Like the other day I was just looking out the window, and my neighbor’s dog was barking—he’s got this little thing that thinks it’s a guard dog—and I started thinking about how I used to get up and get moving without all this fuss. But then it turned into thinking about whether I’d be able to keep up at the warehouse.

So… hopeless, when work isn’t on my mind? I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed it happening separate from all that.
Have you had times when you felt down or lost interest in things, even when there wasn’t anything going on at work to worry about?

I guess… I keep trying to answer that cleanly, but it all loops back to the warehouse. Ever since they changed my hours and put in that new inventory system, I feel like I’m just not keeping up.

I used to be the kind of person who showed up—work, church, whatever I said I’d do. Now I’m missing shifts, missing commitments at church, and then I come home and snap at my family over small things. My daughter said I sounded like her old high school principal the other day—always correcting somebody—and I didn’t even realize I was doing it.

So, down or not interested when work isn’t a worry… I don’t know. The work worry is sitting there most of the time. Some mornings I’ve got my boots on and I just sit there, wondering if I can even make myself face that place.
Have you ever found yourself feeling anxious or worried about work even when there wasn’t an immediate problem, like a specific change or mistake, happening at the time?

Yeah… I think so. It’s like even if nothing new happened that day, I’m still bracing for it. Ever since they changed my hours and put in that inventory system, I feel like I’m falling apart a little.

I’ll be sitting there at home, and I should be getting ready, or thinking about church stuff I said I’d help with—actually, I missed another thing there, which I hate because those folks count on me—and then my mind goes right back to the warehouse. Am I going to mess up, am I too slow, what if I can’t keep up.

Some mornings I’ve already got my work boots on, and I just sit there. Nothing’s happened yet, no mistake, no new change that morning… but I’m still wondering if I can even face the place. And then I get irritated with my family over nothing, which makes me feel worse.
Have you noticed yourself feeling anxious about work even when there’s nothing specific happening at the warehouse that day, like no new changes or mistakes?

Yeah… yes, I have. It’s not even always that something happened that day. I’ll just be there at home, and—well, my wife will be asking if I want coffee, or I’ll notice the grass needs cutting, and then suddenly I’m thinking about the warehouse again.

Ever since they changed my hours and put in that new inventory system, I feel like I’m falling apart. I’m missing shifts, and I’ve missed things at church too, which bothers me because I don’t like letting people down. And then I snap at my family over little things.

Some mornings I’m already in my work boots, just sitting there, no new change, no mistake yet, and I’m wondering if I can even face the place anymore.
Do you find yourself feeling anxious about work even when there’s no clear reason or specific problem to focus on, like on days when everything seems to be going smoothly?

Yeah… I mean, that’s kind of why I came in. It doesn’t even have to be something going wrong right then.

Ever since they changed my warehouse hours and put in that new inventory system, I feel like I’m falling apart. I keep missing shifts, and then I miss things at church too—which bothers me, because I’ve always tried to be dependable there. My wife will say I’m getting sharp with people at home, and she’s right, I snap over stupid little things.

And some mornings I’ll have my work boots on already, just sitting there, and I can’t seem to make myself get up and go. I’m not even thinking of one specific problem exactly… just facing the place feels like too much.
Would you say that you feel anxious or worried about work on most days, even when nothing specific is going wrong?

Most days, yeah… that’s fair to say. It’s not always one particular thing going wrong that morning.

I came in because ever since they changed my warehouse hours and put in that new inventory system, I feel like I’m falling apart. I’m missing shifts, and then it spills over—I miss church commitments too, and I hate that because I’ve known some of those people for years, you know, they expect me to show up. My family’s getting the short end of it too, because I snap at them over little things.

Some mornings I’ve already got my work boots on, and I just sit there looking at the floor, wondering if I can even face the place. So… yes, it’s most days. Even when nothing specific is happening.

patient.answer:
Most days, yeah… that’s fair to say. It’s not always one particular thing going wrong that morning.

I came in because ever since they changed my warehouse hours and put in that new inventory system, I feel like I’m falling apart. I’m missing shifts, and then it spills over—I miss church commitments too, and I hate that because I’ve known some of those people for years, you know, they expect me to show up. My family’s getting the short end of it too, because I snap at them over little things.

Some mornings I’ve already got my work boots on, and I just sit there looking at the floor, wondering if I can even face the place. So… yes, it’s most days. Even when nothing specific is happening.
